ROLL CALL: At 6:11 p.m., on Monday, November 13, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Parks and
Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Chief of Police Kennedy, Principal Planner McCurley

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledged that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

2.  PUBLIC HEARING TO ADOPT ORDINANCE O2M23-4823 APPROVING ZONING TEXT
  AMENDMENT AMD-23-10 (THE COMPREHENSIVE UPDATE TO THE CITY OF
  ALHAMBRA ZONING CODE [TITLE 23 OF THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE]) AND
  ZONING MAP AMENDMENT AMD-23-09 (AN AMENDMENT TO THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  OFFICIAL ZONING MAP); AND A RESOLUTION APPROVING GENERAL PLAN TEXT
  AMENDMENT AMD-23-08 (AN AMENDMENT TO THE LAND USE AND COMMUNITY
  DESIGN CHAPTER OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN, VISION 2040),
  GENERAL PLAN MAP AMENDMENT AMD-23-07 (AN AMENDMENT TO THE CITY OF
  ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN LAND USE MAP), AND INITIAL STUDY/NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION – F2M20-24, N2M23-127, O2M23-4823, R2M23-54

  Principal Planner MCCURLEY made a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerks Office.
  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M23-127 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider a General Plan Map Amendment, General Plan Text Amendment, Zoning
  Map Amendment and Zoning Text Amendment adopting the comprehensive update to the City
  of Alhambra Zoning Code (Title 23 of the Alhambra Municipal Code), an Amendment to the
  City of Alhambra Official Zoning Map, an Amendment to the Land Use and Community Design
  Chapter of the City of Alhambra General Plan, Vision 2040, and an Amendment to the City of
  Alhambra General Plan Land Use Map (the “Project”); and to adopt the Initial Study/Negative
  Declaration for the Project pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). On
  August 10, 2020, the City Council was provided an introduction to the comprehensive Zoning
  Code update project known as CODEALHAMBRA (www.alhambracodeupdate.com). The
  goal of the project being to update the City of Alhambra’s 37-year-old Zoning Code with a
  state of-the-art, flexible, user-friendly Zoning Code that serves as an effective tool to implement
  the community’s vision for the future. The project was then introduced to the Planning
  Commission on December 7, 2020. The public was given opportunity to participate in the
  project in two community workshops held on January 21 and 23, 2021.

  Between August 1, 2022, and December 5, 2022, an overview of the draft Zoning Code was
  presented to the Planning Commission over the course of seven meetings, which were open
  to the public and promoted through several methods, including social media in multiple
  languages. The presentations covered the chapters of the draft Zoning Code, such as permit
  processes, permitted uses, development standards, parking standards, and nonconformities.
  Following these initial presentations on the draft Zoning Code, 42 areas of the proposed
  Zoning Code were identified for further discussion. These became known as “The 42
  Comments.” Discussions of these comments spanned nine meetings between December 19,
  2022 and May 1, 2023. The next four presentations between May 15, 2023 and July 10, 2023
  focused on zone changes and in particular, the rezoning of all of the P (Parking) zone lots to
  another zoning classification. Over the course of these 20 meetings, members of the public
  attended regularly and provided comments on the presentations. Additionally, each meeting
  was also recorded through Zoom and made available to view on the City website and the
  CODEALHAMBRA project website.

  The Planning Commission’s public hearing on the Zoning Code was originally scheduled for
  August 7, 2023 and was continued for the next several meetings (August 21st, September 5th,
  September 18th, October 2nd, and October 16th). Following a presentation on September 18,
  2023, the Planning Commission received public comment and began their deliberations, which
  continued to October 2nd and October 16, 2023. At the October 16, 2023 meeting, by a vote of
  9-0 with one absence, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. 23-20 recommending
  the City Council approve the comprehensive Zoning Code update and associated Zoning and
  General Plan amendment applications with the incorporation of the Planning Commission’s
  recommended changes. The Planning Commission’s recommended revisions to the Zoning
  Code included changes to: use allowances; residential setbacks; maximum building stories
  2
11-13-23
   and heights; minimum residential open space; maximum density; minimum affordable housing
  requirements; public noticing and review authority for Minor Administrative Reviews; time limits
  for appeal periods; as well as incorporation of the existing Residential Planned Development
  Permit process. Staff presented the Planning Commission’s recommended revisions to the
  City Council for consideration. Certain language in the draft Ordinance and Resolution requires
  direction from the Council; specifically, as to whether or not to accept or modify the Planning
  Commission’s recommendations, or to adopt without further revision the draft documents as
  recommended by staff.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ thanked everyone who provided feedback, provided a
  background the City’s RHNA requirements, HCD requirements, suggested making everything
  east of Almansor St. 3-stories high, and discussed allowing housing in the EMC. She further
  discussed Planning Commission recommendations on comments no. 7, 14, 16, 17, 27, 28,
  and additional recommendations 2, 3, and 5. She noted that the Planning Commission and
  Staff were in alignment on these points. Ms. PÉREZ made a motion to approve Planning
  Commission recommendations 7, 14, 16, 17, 27, 28, to approve additional recommendations
  2, 3, and 5, and to change the building height limit to 3 stories in the EMC. Councilmember
  LEE requested for the Council to provide their comments prior to the Council voting on specific
  Planning Commission recommendations. Ms. PÉREZ clarified the points she included in her
  motion and were supported by staff as well as the Planning Commission as laid out in staff’s
  presentation. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER seconded Ms. PÉREZ’s motion. Ms.
  LEE continued to request that Council address each item individually before taking a vote.
  Mayor MAZA, Ms. LEE, and Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss her motion, the order of
  Council’s discussion.
  4
11-13-23
   Councilmember MALONEY thanked everyone who participated in the meeting tonight and
  acknowledged Ms. Pérez’s motion and the recommendations which were agreed upon by Staff
  and the Planning Commission. He discussed the potential risks of adopting a zoning code
  update that did not comply with State law with regards to RHNA and HCD. Mr. MALONEY
  further discussed Council’s ability to approve the Zoning Code while continuing to monitor and
  make changes as needs arise in the future. He agreed with Ms. Pérez’s assessment regarding
  the community’s concerns and added that Council should preserve the height limits that were
  acceptable to the community while still fulfilling their RHNA goals.

  Ms. LEE acknowledged the public comments made at tonight’s meeting, noted that over time,
  change was sometimes necessary. She expressed concerns with height limits and setbacks
  for buildings. She made reference to a document which a member of the public referred to in
  conversation but that she could not produce which suggested that based on a different
  calculation the high density was not required and that 2 or 3 story buildings were sufficient in
  the EMC and along Valley Blvd. She expressed that she was not comfortable approving 4 or
  5 story building heights unless there was data presented to justify it.

  Ms. LEE asked for clarification for comment #6 regarding the calculation for building setbacks
  and inquired about height requirements in certain areas of the City as it related to the setback.
  Director of Community Development HO and Ms. LEE had an in-depth conversation regarding
  the Planning Commission recommendation for calculation of a 30-degree plane from side
  yards which would determine the setback of additional stories on an adjacent building,
  setbacks to rear yards, driveway width, additional buffer zones in new draft code, and the ways
  in which the recommendation would apply to developments on Valley Blvd. and East Main St.
  Ms. LEE stated that her motion would include the acceptance of the Planning Commission
  recommendation for the 30-degree plane calculation for setbacks for side yards as well as
  rear yards.

  Ms. LEE and Mr. HO continued to discuss the zoning map shown in staff’s presentation, the
  ways in which the zoning along Valley Blvd would affect the neighboring RH neighborhoods,
  the building heights as dictated by zoning on Valley Blvd, and the specific area between
  Atlantic, Woodward, Commonwealth, and Chapel where building heights would be 6 stories
  as opposed to other areas outside of that boundary where the maximum height would be 5
  stories.

  Ms. LEE and Mr. HO went on to discuss Comment #23 and the Planning Commission
  recommendations pertaining to the building heights in the EMC. Mr. HO clarified that building
  height was dependent on the zoning of each individual property. Ms. LEE expressed concerns
  regarding tall buildings adjacent to residential neighborhoods. He explained that although the
  Planning Commission recommended a reduced maximum of 4 stories at 55ft, that the building
  height was dependent on whether it was adjacent to an RM or RH property in which case the
  buffer zone would be applied. Ms. LEE and Mr. HO further discussed her suggestions
  regarding setbacks and its affect on the overall building design. After discussion, Ms. LEE
  stated that she would later make a motion for a maximum building height of 3 stories or 2
  stories above ground with a 30-degree plane setback. Mr. HO explained the Planning
  Commission recommendation and that the building height depended on the zoning of each
  property and Ms. LEE stated that she could not tell from the map provided and that she wanted
  to ensure that R1 neighborhoods were not impacted by proposal.

  The Council discussed the motion that was on the floor as made by Ms. PÉREZ. City Attorney
  MONTES clarified that Council could move forward with an approval of the Ordinance and
  Draft Zoning Code if there was a consensus among them on each point or if there were minor
  adjustments to the comments provided. However, he added that if Council made substantial
  changes or made recommendations that were different from any provided by Staff or the
  5
11-13-23
   Planning Commission, then staff may need to revise the document and present it at a later
  meeting for approval. Mr. MAZA, Mr. MALONEY, and Mr. MONTES discussed Council’s ability
  to state their consensus on an aspect of the Zoning Code without the need for a formal vote
  approving it. Mr. MOTES added that staff needed further clarification regarding the specific
  building height of stories with regards to comment #23.

  Ms. PÉREZ made a motion to also include comment #23 and reforming the height
  requirements on the East Main Corridor (EMC) to make everything west of Almansor St. 5-
  stories at 75ft, to allow for 3-stories at 40ft everything east of Almansor St., and to allow for
  housing in those areas up to the border of the City. Mr. MONTES asked if there was consensus
  and there was no verbal response. At the request of Ms. LEE, Ms. PÉREZ clarified restated
  her motions.

  Ms. LEE, Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, and Mr. MAZA discussed if the specific number of stories
  included underground levels or mixed-use levels. Mr. HO clarified that staff defined stories as
  anything above grade.

  Mr. MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed the effect maximum building heights might have on the
  approved Housing Element. Mr. MALONEY stated that he agreed that it should be extended
  to Almansor St. Ms. LEE indicated that she would make a substitute motion. She again
  discussed an aforementioned document which demonstrated that the City had an overage of
  housing units accounted for and that therefore the city could clearly lower the maximum
  building height from Chapel to Almansor because it was not required. Mr. MONTES clarified
  the data to which Ms. Lee referred to, explaining that HCD required a buffer of 15% - 20%
  above the RHNA goals in order to accommodate for projects which do not build to the
  anticipated density which would in turn require the City to up-zone other areas of the City. Mr.
  HO further clarified that the Housing Element had a buffer of 17% of housing units planned.

  Ms. LEE continued to express her concerns with building heights of 4 or 5 stories in proximity
  to residential zones. She expressed that she would accept 3 stories from Chapel to West
  Granada but that her first motion was for a maximum of 25ft above ground, allowing for parking
  garages to be set below grade. She further alluded to the upcoming Historic Preservation
  Ordinance and explained that 4 or 5 stories would contradict the effort to preserve potentially
  historic districts which border the EMC. She continued to reiterate her points regarding
  preservation of the traditional appeal of neighborhoods along the EMC.

  Mayor MAZA referred back to Ms. Pérez’s motion which was seconded by Ms. Andrade-
  Stadler and requested a roll call. Ms. LEE requested clarification regarding Comment #23 in
  the motion. Ms. LEE requested the ability to make a substitute motion. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER withdrew her second to Ms. Pérez’s motion. Ms. PÉREZ again restated her motion.

  Ms. LEE offered a substitute motion regarding revisions to building height in the EMC to allow
  for 2 stories at 25ft. above ground level from Chapel Ave. to the west side of Granada Ave. or
  3-stories with a thirty-degree plane for a side yard or rear yard setbacks. Ms. LEE and Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER discussed allowing for subterranean parking. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr.
  MONTES clarified that zoning codes did not typically dictate below ground levels and it was
  therefore not included in the number of stories. Ms. PEREZ restated her previous motion for 3
  stories and reiterated her points.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER recommended bringing down the number of stories west of
  Almansor St. from 5-stories to 4-stories. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER asked if Ms. PÉREZ would
  consider amending her motion to reduce building heights. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr. MALONEY
  stated that 5 stories was consistent with the rest of the CBD, that the lots west of Granada
  were deeper and had less of an impact on residential homes, and that it addressed the
  concerns she had heard from residents.
  6
11-13-23
   Ms. LEE offered an second substitute motion for the maximum building heights from Chapel
  Ave. to west of Granada to be set at 3 stories at 35 feet above ground with the 30 degree
  encroachment plane for a setback from a side or rear yard. She stated that there would be no
  housing allowed east of Granada with maximum building heights of 2 stories. She continued
  to reiterate her points supporting lower building heights.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER inquired about the height limits on the current mixed-use
  development at the old public library site and Director of Community Development HO
  provided clarification stating that the height limit was 4 stories and the development had
  varying heights. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss her motion
  and building heights, the ways in which previous topics were addressed in other comments
  provided by the Planning Commission or Staff.

  Mr. MAZA restated that motion on the floor and inquired if there was a second. Ms. LEE
  continued to restate her second substitute motion and discuss the points she made. Mr. MAZA
  clarified the differences between Ms. Lee’s second substitute motion and Ms. Pérez’s motion,
  namely the differences of maximum height between Chapel and Granada. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER seconded Ms. Lee’s second substitute motion.

  Action Taken:  The Council allowed for 3-stories or 35 feet above ground with a
  third-degree plane for a side yard from Chapel Ave. to the west side of Granada Ave.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ
  Noes:  MALONEY, MAZA
  Absent:  NONE

  Discussion: Mr. MONTES noted that the motion did not address the other points of the
  draft Zoning Code and that it only addressed the area between Chapel and Granada. Ms.
  PÉREZ reiterated her previous motion to approve the uncontested comments and expressed
  concern with taking each item one at a time, noting the time constraints of the current meeting
  and remaining Agenda items. Mr. MAZA agreed with Ms. Pérez but added that the only way
  to get through all the information was to take each point individually. Mr. MALONEY noted that
  he was not clear on the motion from the last vote and discussed building height concerns with
  CBD and EMC. He referred to Ms. Pérez’s original motion which addressed several concerns
  from the public as well as the comments provided by the Planning Commission and Staff. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested bringing back this item to the December meeting.

  Mayor MAZA thanked the Planning Commission and members of the public for their work on
  the zoning code update. He went on to discuss State Housing requirements, Council’s
  responsibility, the character of the City, and the involvement of the residents. Mr. MAZA
  reiterated his support for Ms. Pérez’s original motion for 5 stories at 75 feet between Chapel
  and Almansor, and 3 stories at 40 feet from Almansor to Granada or the City boundary.

  Mr. MAZA stated that Council would bring the item back to the December 11, 2023 meeting.
  Mr. MONTES clarified that a motion was still required. Ms. PÉREZ requested that staff bring
  back a presentation with a simplified information and a list of what is pending and additional
  information on the City’s RHNA requirements. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to continue
  the item, which was seconded by Mr. MALONEY.

  Action Taken:  The Council continued this item to the December 11, 2023, Council meeting
  at 6:00 p.m.

  7
11-13-23
   Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATION

3.  COUNCIL DIRECTION ON ALHAMBRA COMMUNITY CENTER DESIGN – F2M22-65,
  M2M23-197

  Director of Parks & Recreation MACIAS delivered a staff report and Tara BEEBE, KFA, made
  a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s Office. City staff worked with KFA Architects
  and Environmental Science Associates to develop the Environmental Impact Report (EIR) to
  meet the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) requirements. On October 25, 2023, a
  public community meeting requesting input on the Alhambra Community Center building
  designs was conducted. As part of the community engagement process, staff distributed door
  hangers to residents, businesses, and churches in the surrounding area. In addition, the
  community was made aware of the community meeting through social media outlets and
  provided a survey via survey monkey. Fifty community members attended the meeting and
  198 completed an online survey. At the public outreach meeting, members of the community
  provided input as to what building and landscape features they preferred. In addition, they
  were asked to select the building rendering they preferred the most. The online survey mirrored
  the community meeting request for input. The City was also in discussions with the Alhambra
  Unified School District so that the street may be vacated to allow for better use of the
  community center parcel and expanded water recapture infrastructure at the north portion of
  the City parcel. Staff evaluated the results of the community meeting survey and the online
  survey and will present the results to the City Council. Staff sought Council direction on the
  building scheme and elements to help finalize the project description for the EIR.

  Public Comment:
  1) Michael McCULLUM, W. Alhambra Rd., expressed concerns with the concept design and
  recommended preserving part of the building.

  2) Bert NG expressed excitement for a new community center and recommended utilizing the
  existing architecture of the current building.

  3) Jennifer NG expressed concern with the entire building being demolished and recommended
  preserving part of the building.

  4) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., recommending preserving part of the existing
  building and noted that he is in favor of some of the conceptual designs as well.

  5) Shirley TATSUNO, S. Fifth St., expressed her preference for a more modern building but also
  questioned why the historical aspect was taken away in the conceptual drawings.

  6) Chris OLSON, via zoom, recommended declining both conceptual designs and expressed
  support to preserve the historical architecture of the current building. She also submitted her
  comments on behalf of the Alhambra Historical Society via email, which are on file in the City
  Clerk’s office.

  7) Melissa MICHELSON, via zoom, expressed her excitement for a community center but
  expressed concern with the proposed conceptual designs.

  8) Oscar AMARO, via zoom, expressed sympathy with the choice in front of the Council,
  expressed support to preserve the historical architecture of the current building. He also
  submitted his comments via email on behalf of the Alhambra Preservation Group, which are
  on file in the City Clerk’s office.
  8
11-13-23
   9) Cliff BENDER, via zoom, expressed concern with the public input on the two conceptual
  designs and noted the lack of information included in the agenda packet.

  10) Joyce AMARO, via zoom, expressed support to preserve the historical architecture of the
  current building.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE expressed support to preserve at least a portion
  of the current building, noted that preserving the interior of the building would not be practical
  for its new use, and requested that the architect look into additional design ideas that would
  include preserving the current architecture. Chuck CALLOWAY, Calloway Design, provided
  clarification.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER noted the current concerns with the existing building
  and envisioned a mixture of modern touches along with preserving the historical aspects of
  the building.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ discussed how important the future community center would be for the
  community, noted that the Council sub-committee was heavily involved in the conceptual
  designs, and inquired if there were any constraints faced with the design process. Ms. BEEBE
  responded to questions.

  Ms. PÉREZ noted the time constraints of getting the project completed due to the funding
  received, noted the design selected tonight will not be the final design of the building, and
  inquired about the EIR process for the project. City Attorney MONTES provided clarification.

  Councilmember MALONEY discussed incorporating as much of the old building as possible
  into the new design.

  Mayor MAZA discussed the challenges of utilizing some of the historical aspects of the
  building, noted that there is a small amount of funding to complete the project, and discussed
  the timeline to finalize the design of the building.

  Action Taken:  City Council selected Community Center building design option
  Scheme I. “Around the Camp Fire” with the red tile roof, to assist in development of the
  Environmental Impact Report (EIR) project description and provided feedback on the building
  design elements and landscape features; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M23-197)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4-19)

All other items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item Nos. 4, 15, and 19, were
considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

4.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: INSTALLATION OF PEDESTRIAN COUNTDOWN SIGNAL HEAD
  SYSTEMS PROJECT AT VARIOUS INTERSECTIONS THROUGHOUT THE CITY (HSIP-
  5130(022)) – F2M23-73, N2M23-137

  Staff recently secured approval from the California Department of Transportation for the
  HSIP-5130(022) Install Pedestrian Countdown Signal Head Systems Project. The project
  9
11-13-23
   consisted of installing countdown signal heads at various intersections throughout the City.
  The project was submitted to the Department of Transportation under the Highway Safety
  Improvement Program Cycle 9. It was selected for funding in the amount of $876,000. Plans

  DETERMINE THIS ACTION IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA – F2M23-7, O2M23-4812, O2M23-
  4822

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M23-4812, imposing a
  temporary moratorium on so called “renovictions,” through December 31, 2023. On September
  30, 2023, SB 567 was signed by the Governor. SB 567 revised certain tenant protections in
  State law which address the concerns that the City’s moratorium was intended to address.
  However, those protections would not take effect until April 1, 2024. At the October 9, 2023
  City Council meeting, the City Council directed that an amendment to Ordinance No.
  O2M23-4812 be agendized to extend the term of the temporary moratorium on renovictions
  until the tenant protections of SB 567 become effective. The City reviewed the environmental
  impacts of this Ordinance under the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources
  Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code
  of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). This Ordinance was not subject to further
  review environmental review because: (1) it would not result in a direct or reasonably
  foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15060(c)(2);
  (2) there was no possibility that this Ordinance themselves may have a significant effect on
  the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) the Ordinance, by itself, do not
  constitute a “project” as defined in the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15378). The
  Ordinance was for general policies and procedure-making.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON, 105. N. Cordova St., expressed support for the
  recommended action until state law takes effect and referred to Item No. 15, noting he was in
  agreement with keeping the current City crossing guards as City employees and using the
